value.zh: 在郡垂二十年，討平叛賊，功績修理。
value.en: For almost twenty years in the prefecture he crushed rebels and ran an orderly administration.
value.literal: In the commandery nearly twenty years, he suppressed and pacified rebel bandits; his achievements and administration were orderly.

value.zh: 召還武昌，為繞帳督。
value.en: Recalled to Wuchang, he commanded the headquarters guard.
value.literal: He was summoned back to Wuchang and became commander of the tent guard.

value.zh: 時太常潘浚掌荊州事，重安長陳留舒燮有罪下獄，浚嘗失燮，欲置之於法。
value.en: Minister Pan Jun then governed Jingzhou; Shu Xie of Chenliu, magistrate of Chong’an, stood accused—Pan Jun had old grievances and meant to punish him.
value.literal: At that time Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun oversaw Jing Province affairs; the magistrate of Chong’an, Shu Xie of Chenliu, was guilty and imprisoned; Jun had once faulted Xie and wished to apply the law to him.

value.zh: 論者多為有言，浚猶不釋。
value.en: Many pleaded for Shu Xie; Pan Jun still refused to relent.
value.literal: Though many debaters spoke on his behalf, Jun still would not release him.

value.zh: 鄰謂浚曰："舒伯膺兄弟爭死，海內義之，以為美談，仲膺又奉國舊意。
value.en: Sun Lin told Pan Jun: The Shu brothers once vied to die for honor—the empire admired it—and Zhongying still carries that loyalty.
value.literal: Lin said to Jun, The Shu brothers Boying contended to die for each other—the realm praised their righteousness as a fine tale—and Zhongying moreover embodies the state’s former intentions.

value.zh: 今君殺其子弟，若天下一統，青蓋北巡，中州士人必問仲膺繼嗣，答者雲潘承明殺燮，於事何如?"浚意即解，燮用得濟。
value.en: If you execute his kin and the empire is someday reunited, the north will ask after Zhongying’s heir—and answering Pan Jun killed Shu Xie will shame you. Pan Jun relented and Shu Xie was spared.
value.literal: Now if you kill his sons and nephews, should the realm unite and the imperial canopy tour north, gentlemen of the Central Plains will surely ask who succeeds Zhongying—if the answer is Pan Chengming killed Xie, how will that stand? Jun’s intent immediately loosened, and Xie obtained deliverance.

value.zh: 〈《博物志》曰：仲膺名邵。
value.en: 〈Bowuzhi: Zhongying’s personal name was Shao.
value.literal: 〈The Bowuzhi states: Zhongying’s given name was Shao.

value.zh: 初，伯膺亲友为人所杀，仲膺为报怨。
value.en: Boying’s kin had been murdered; Zhongying took revenge.
value.literal: At first Boying’s relatives were murdered by someone; Zhongying avenged the grievance.

value.zh: 事觉，兄弟争死，皆得免。
value.en: When discovered they argued over who should die; both were pardoned.
value.literal: When the affair was discovered the brothers vied to die; both were spared.

value.zh: 袁术时，邵为阜陵长。
value.en: Under Yuan Shu, Shao was magistrate of Fuling.
value.literal: During Yuan Shu’s time Shao was magistrate of Fuling.

value.zh: 亦见江表传。〉
value.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan records the same.〉
value.literal: It is also seen in the Jiangbiao zhuan.〉

value.zh: 鄰遷夏口沔中督、威遠將軍，所居任職。
value.en: Sun Lin rose to middle-Han–Xiakou inspector and General Who Deters the Distance, performing solid service.
value.literal: Lin was promoted inspector of Xiakou and the central Mian and General Who Deters the Distance, carrying out his duties where stationed.

value.zh: 赤烏十二年卒。
value.en: He died in Chiwu 12.
value.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Chiwu.

value.zh: 子苗嗣。
value.en: His son Sun Miao inherited.
value.literal: His son Miao succeeded.

value.zh: 苗弟旅及叔父安、熙、績，皆歷列位。
value.en: Sun Miao’s brother Sun Lü and uncles Sun An, Sun Xi, and Sun Ji all served in turn.
value.literal: Miao’s younger brother Lü and uncles An, Xi, and Ji all held successive offices.

value.zh: 〈吴历曰：邻又有子曰述，为武昌督，平荆州事。
value.en: 〈The Wu li notes another son, Shu, who commanded Wuchang and Jingzhou affairs.
value.literal: 〈The Wu li states: Lin also had a son named Shu, who was inspector of Wuchang and handled Jing Province affairs.

value.zh: 震，无难督。
value.en: Sun Zhen held the colonelcy Who Has No Difficulty.
value.literal: Zhen, Colonel Who Has No Difficulty.

value.zh: 谐，城门校尉。
value.en: Sun Xie was colonel of the Capital Gates.
value.literal: Xie, colonel of the Capital Gates.

value.zh: 歆，乐乡督。
value.en: Sun Xin commanded Lexiang.
value.literal: Xin, inspector of Lexiang.

value.zh: 震后御晋军，与张悌俱死。
value.en: Sun Zhen later faced the Jin host and fell beside Zhang Ti.
value.literal: Later Zhen opposed the Jin army and died together with Zhang Ti.

value.zh: 贲曾孙惠，字德施。
value.en: Sun Ben’s great-grandson Sun Hui, styled Deshi.
value.literal: Ben’s great-grandson Hui, courtesy name Deshi.

value.zh: 《惠别传》曰：惠好学有才智，晋永宁元年，赴齐王冏义，以功封晋兴侯，辟大司马贼曹属。
value.en: His appendix: Sun Hui was bookish and clever; in Jin Yongning 1 he joined Prince Sima Jiong’s righteous army, earned the marquisate of Jinxing, and entered the grand marshal’s criminal bureau.
value.literal: The Separate Biography of Hui states: Hui loved learning and had talent and judgment; in the first year of Yongning of Jin he answered Prince Qi of Qi’s call to righteousness and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Jinxing and summoned aide in the bandit bureau of the Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 冏骄矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Sima Jiong grew arrogant and wasteful and forfeited the empire’s trust.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, presumptuous, and extravagant; the realm lost hope in him.

value.zh: 惠献言於冏，讽以五难、四不可，劝令委让万机，归籓青岱，辞甚深切。
value.en: Sun Hui remonstrated with the five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to surrender power and retire to his Shandong fief—in biting terms.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using allegories of five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to yield the myriad affairs of state and return to his fief on Qing and Dai—the words were trenchant indeed.

value.zh: 冏不能纳，顷之果败。
value.en: Sima Jiong would not listen and soon fell.
value.literal: Jiong could not accept it; shortly afterward he indeed fell.

value.zh: 成都王颖召为大将军参军。
value.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying named him grand general’s aide.
value.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the Grand General.

value.zh: 是时颖将有事於长沙，以陆机为前锋都督。
value.en: Sima Ying was preparing a Changsha campaign and made Lu Ji vanguard commander.
value.literal: At that time Ying was about to undertake affairs at Changsha and made Lu Ji advance commander.

value.zh: 惠与机乡里亲厚，忧其致祸，谓之曰：“子盍让都督於王粹乎？”
value.en: Sun Hui, Lu Ji’s townsman and friend, feared ruin for him and asked: Why not give the command to Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same village as Ji and close to him; fearing disaster for Ji, he said to him, Why not yield the commander’s post to Wang Cui?

value.zh: 机曰：“将谓吾避贼首鼠，更速其害。”
value.en: Lu Ji answered: They would call me a coward—that would only hasten disaster.
value.literal: Ji said, People would say I shrink from the enemy like a rat—that would hasten my ruin.

value.zh: 机寻被戮，二弟云、耽亦见杀，惠甚伤恨之。
value.en: Lu Ji was soon executed with his brothers Yun and Dan; Sun Hui mourned bitterly.
value.literal: Ji was shortly afterward executed; his two younger brothers Yun and Dan were also killed—Hui deeply grieved for them.

value.zh: 永兴元年，乘舆幸鄴，司空东海王越治兵下邳，惠以书干越，诡其姓名，自称南岳逸民秦祕之，勉以勤王匡世之略，辞义甚美。
value.en: In Yongxing 1 the court moved toward Ye; Prince Donghai Sima Yue trained troops at Xiapi. Sun Hui wrote under the pseudonym Southern Mountain hermit Qin Mizhi, urging him to rescue the throne.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongxing the imperial carriage favored Ye; Minister of Works Prince Donghai Sima Yue drilled troops at Xiapi—Hui wrote to Yue under a false name, calling himself the South Mountain recluse Qin Mizhi, urging with handsome phrases the strategy of aiding the king and restoring the age.

value.zh: 越省其书，榜题道衢，招求其人。
value.en: Sima Yue posted the essay at crossroads and hunted for the author.
value.literal: Yue read his letter, posted the title on the roads, and sought the man.

value.zh: 惠乃出见，越即以为记室参军，专掌文疏，豫参谋议。
value.en: Sun Hui revealed himself; Sima Yue made him secretary-aide for drafts and planning.
value.literal: Hui then came forward to meet him; Yue immediately made him secretary-aide, solely in charge of documents and participating in counsel.

value.zh: 每造书檄，越或驿马催之，应命立成，皆有辞旨。
value.en: When Sima Yue needed edicts he sometimes sent post riders—Sun Hui composed them on demand, always elegant.
value.literal: Whenever he drafted letters or proclamations, Yue sometimes sent relay horses to hurry him; he answered the summons on the spot and finished at once, each piece having polished rhetoric.

value.zh: 累迁显职，后为广武将军、安丰内史。
value.en: He climbed to high office and ended as campaigning General Who Displays Might and interior minister of Anfeng.
value.literal: He rose through prominent posts and later became General Who Displays Might on Campaign and interior minister of Anfeng.

value.zh: 年四十七卒。
value.en: He died at forty-seven.
value.literal: He died at forty-seven.

value.zh: 惠文翰凡數十首。
value.en: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.〉
value.literal: Hui’s literary compositions number several tens of pieces in all.〉

value.zh: 孫桓字叔武，河之子也。
value.en: Sun Huan, styled Shuwo, was Sun He’s son.
value.literal: Sun Huan, courtesy name Shuwo, was He's son.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：河有四子。
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun He had four sons.)
value.literal: 〈《Wu shu》 states: He had four sons.

value.zh: 长助，曲阿长。
value.en: Eldest Sun Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.
value.literal: The eldest Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.

value.zh: 次谊，海盐长。
value.en: Next Sun Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.
value.literal: Next Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.

value.zh: 并早卒。
value.en: Both died young.
value.literal: Both died early.

value.zh: 次桓，仪容端正，器怀聪朗，博学强记，能论议应对，权常称为宗室颜渊，擢为武卫都尉。
value.en: Sun Huan was handsome, quick-witted, learned, and eloquent—Sun Quan called him the clan’s Yan Hui and made him colonel of the martial guard.
value.literal: Next Huan, whose bearing was correct, whose mind was bright, who studied broadly and memorized strongly, could debate and reply—Quan always called him the Zengzi of the imperial clan and promoted him colonel of the martial guard.

value.zh: 从讨关羽於华容，诱羽餘党，得五千人，牛马器械甚众。〉
value.en: He joined the strike on Guan Yu at Huarong, lured five thousand of his stragglers, and captured huge herds and gear.〉
value.literal: He followed in campaigning against Guan Yu at Huarong, enticed Yu's remaining followers, gained five thousand men, and oxen, horses, and equipment were very numerous.〉

value.zh: 年二十五，拜安東中郎將，與陸遜共拒劉備。
value.en: At twenty-five he was General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East beside Lu Xun against Liu Bei.
value.literal: At age twenty-five he was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East and together with Lu Xun resisted Liu Bei.

value.zh: 備軍眾甚盛，彌山盈谷，桓投力奮命。
value.en: Liu Bei’s host covered hills and dales; Sun Huan threw everything into the line.
value.literal: Bei's army host was very strong, filling mountains and valleys; Huan devoted his strength and risked his life.

value.zh: 與遜戮力，備遂敗走。
value.en: He and Lu Xun strained together until Liu Bei broke and ran.
value.literal: Together with Xun he exerted joint effort; Bei thereupon fled in defeat.

value.zh: 桓斬上
value.en: Sun Huan severed the Shanggui—
value.literal: Huan cut Shang—

value.en: ms. dou
value.literal: (variant dou)

value.en: ms. kui
value.literal: (variant kui)

value.zh: 道，截其徑要。
value.en: —route and seized the defiles.
value.literal: —road and intercepted the vital narrows.

value.zh: 備逾山越險，僅乃得免，忿恚歎曰："吾昔初至京城，桓尚小兒，而今迫孤乃至此也!"桓以功拜建武將軍，封丹徒侯，下督牛港，作橫江塢，會卒。
value.en: Liu Bei scrambled through the hills barely alive and swore: “When I first saw Jingcheng, Sun Huan was a boy—now he corners me like this!” Sun Huan earned General Who Establishes Martial Might, marquis of Dantu, command at Niugang, built the Hengjiang redoubt, then died.
value.literal: Bei crossed mountains and passed defiles, barely escaping; angrily sighing he said: "When I first came to Jingcheng, Huan was still a small child—yet now he presses me to this!" Huan for merit was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might, enfeoffed Marquis of Dantu, directed Niugang below, built Hengjiang rampart, and happened to die.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：桓弟俊，字叔英，性度恢弘，才经文武，为定武中郎将，屯戍薄落，赤乌十三年卒。
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: younger brother Sun Jun, styled Shuying, genial and able in letters and arms—General Who Fixes Martial Might at Boluo—died Chiwu 13.)
value.literal: 〈《Wu shu》 states: Huan's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Shuying, by nature was spacious in capacity and accomplished in civil and military arts—General Who Fixes Martial Might, garrisoning Boluo; died thirteenth year of Chiwu.

value.zh: 长子建袭爵，平虏将军。
value.en: Eldest Sun Jian inherited as General Who Pacifies Captives.
value.literal: Eldest son Jian inherited the noble rank—General Who Pacifies Captives.

value.zh: 少子慎，镇南将军。
value.en: Younger Sun Shen became General Who Guards the South.
value.literal: Younger son Shen, General Who Guards the South.

value.zh: 慎子丞，字显世。
value.en: Sun Shen’s son Sun Cheng, styled Xianshi.
value.literal: Shen's son Cheng, courtesy name Xianshi.

value.zh: 文士传曰：丞好学，有文章，作萤火赋行於世。
value.en: (The Wenshi zhuan: Sun Cheng loved books and wrote the Firefly Fu.)
value.literal: 《Wenshi zhuan》 states: Cheng loved learning and had literary skill; he composed the Rhapsody on Fireflies which circulated in the world.

value.zh: 为黄门侍郎，与顾荣俱为侍臣。
value.en: He was a yellow-gates gentleman alongside Gu Rong.
value.literal: He was Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and together with Gu Rong both were attending ministers.

value.zh: 归命世内侍多得罪尤，惟荣、丞独获全。
value.en: When Wu yielded, most palace attendants paid with their lives—only Gu Rong and Sun Cheng survived.
value.literal: In the generation that submitted to the decree, many inner attendants incurred blame and penalty—only Rong and Cheng alone achieved preservation.

value.zh: 常使二人记事，丞答顾问，乃下诏曰：“自今已后，用侍郎皆当如今宗室丞、顾荣畴也。”
value.en: The Jin ruler often consulted them and decreed: Future gentlemen-attendants must match Sun Cheng and Gu Rong.
value.literal: He constantly had the two men keep records; Cheng answered inquiries—thereupon an edict was issued: From now on, appointed gentlemen of the attending suite should all be like the imperial-clan Cheng and Gu Rong here.

value.zh: 吴平赴洛，为范阳涿令，甚有称绩。
value.en: After the conquest he served as magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang with a fine record.
value.literal: When Wu was pacified he went to Luoyang and became magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang—he had very praised achievements.

value.zh: 永安中，陆机为成都王大都督，请丞为司马，与机俱被害。〉
value.en: In Yongan Lu Ji made him staff officer on Prince Chengdu’s campaign—they died together.〉
value.literal: During Yongan Lu Ji was grand marshal to Prince Chengdu and invited Cheng as marshal—together with Ji he met murder.〉

value.zh: 張昭字子布，彭城人也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao, styled Zibu, hailed from Pengcheng.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Zibu, was a man of Pengcheng.

value.zh: 少好學，善隸書，從白侯子安受《左氏春秋》，博覽眾書，與琅邪趙昱、東海王朗俱發名友善。
value.en: As a youth he loved books, wrote a fine clerical hand, studied the Zuo commentary under Bai Hou Zi’an, read omnivorously, and made his name alongside Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai.
value.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at clerical script, received Zuo's Spring and Autumn from Bai Hou Zi'an, read widely among texts, and together with Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai rose to fame as friendly associates.

value.zh: 弱冠察孝廉，不就。
value.en: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt at his capping, he refused appointment.
value.literal: At the capping age he was investigated as filially pious and incorrupt but did not take office.

value.zh: 與朗共論舊君諱事，州裡才士陳琳等皆稱善之。
value.en: He argued with Wang Lang over taboos for former rulers; local talents such as Chen Lin praised his performance.
value.literal: Together with Lang he debated the affair of tabooing former lords; talented men of the commandery such as Chen Lin all praised them.

value.zh: 〈时汝南主簿应劭议宜为旧君讳，论者皆互有异同，事在《风俗通》。
value.en: 〈Ying Shao of Runan had argued for tabooing former masters; the dispute is recorded in the Fengsu tong.)
value.literal: 〈At that time Ying Shao, chief clerk of Runan, argued one ought taboo former lords; debaters differed from one another—the affair is in Fengsu tong.

value.zh: 昭著论曰：“客有见大国之议，士君子之论，云起元建武已来，旧君名讳五十六人，以为后生不得协也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A certain visitor had examined the debates of a great state and the arguments of learned gentlemen. He said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later generations could no longer use names with the same sounds.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A guest had seen the deliberations of a great state and the discussions of gentlemen, and said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty, there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later-born people could not use matching sounds.

value.zh: 取乎经论，譬诸行事，义高辞丽，甚可嘉羡。
value.en: Drawn from canonical gloss and matched to precedent, the rhetoric glows—yet something troubles me.
value.literal: Taking from the classics and commentaries, comparing to deeds performed, the righteousness is lofty and phrases lovely—greatly to be admired.

value.zh: 愚意褊浅，窃有疑焉。
value.en: Forgive a shallow mind—I cannot quite agree.
value.literal: My foolish thought is narrow and shallow—I privately harbor doubt.

value.zh: 盖乾坤剖分，万物定形，肇有父子君臣之经。
value.en: Once heaven and earth divided and creation took shape, the bonds of parent and child, ruler and subject, appeared.
value.literal: In general when Heaven and Earth split apart and the myriad things fixed their forms, there began the constant pattern of father and son, lord and minister.

value.zh: 故圣人顺天之性，制礼尚敬，在三之义，君实食之，在丧之哀，君亲临之，厚莫重焉，恩莫大焉，诚臣子所尊仰，万夫所天恃，焉得而同之哉？
value.en: The sage fashioned ritual from heaven’s nature: lords feed us under the “three that endure”; they mourn with us—nothing outweighs that debt. How can subjects rank them with ordinary kin?
value.literal: Therefore the sage complies with heaven's nature, institutes ritual and esteems reverence; in the duty of the three the lord truly nourishes; in mourning's grief the lord personally attends—the thickness cannot be heavier, the grace cannot be greater—truly what ministers and sons revere and myriad men rely on—how can they be equated?

value.zh: 然亲亲有衰，尊尊有杀，故礼服上不尽高祖，下不尽玄孙。
value.en: Yet kinship weakens by generation and mourning scales down—hence hemp stops short of the fifth grandfather above and the fifth grandson below.
value.literal: Yet intimacy toward kin has degrees of decline; reverence toward superiors has steps of reduction—therefore mourning garments upward do not exhaust great-great-grandfather, downward do not exhaust great-great-grandchild.

value.zh: 又传记四世而缌麻，服之穷也；
value.en: Genealogies say after four generations one wears only thin hemp.
value.literal: Moreover transmitted records: four generations and thin hemp—end of garments;

value.zh: 五世袒免，降杀同姓也；
value.en: After five generations one merely bares head and wrist—the mourning grade fades even within the clan.
value.literal: five generations shed turban and fringe—reduced severity toward same surname;

value.zh: 六世而亲属竭矣。
value.en: By the sixth generation kinship ends.
value.literal: six generations and kinship ties are exhausted.

value.zh: 又曲礼有不逮事之义则不讳，不讳者，盖名之谓，属绝之义，不拘於协，况乃古君五十六哉！
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette also exempts those who never served a lord from tabooing him—that ends obligation to a mere name. If distant kin need not rhyme away syllables, why taboo scores of dead kings?
value.literal: Moreover the Summary of Etiquette has the sense that if one did not succeed to service there is no taboo—no taboo refers to personal names; meaning of severed connection is not bound by harmonizing—how much more fifty-six ancient lords!

value.zh: 邾子会盟，季友来归，不称其名，咸书字者，是时鲁人嘉之也。
value.en: When the Zhu ruler met allies and Jiyou came home, the classic wrote his style, not his name—Lu admired the tact.
value.literal: The lord of Zhu at covenant assembly, Jiyou came to return—his name was not called; all were written with style—at that time the people of Lu praised it.

value.zh: 何解臣子为君父讳乎？
value.en: So why insist clerks taboo every syllable of old patrons?
value.literal: How explain ministers and sons tabooing for lord and father?

value.zh: 周穆王讳满，至定王时有王孙满者，其为大夫，是臣协君也。
value.en: Zhou King Mu banned “Man,” yet under King Ding a minister Wangsun Man served—a subject bore the sovereign’s taboo.
value.literal: King Mu of Zhou tabooed Man; when it reached King Ding there was Wangsun Man who was grand officer—that is a minister harmonizing with his lord.

value.zh: 又厉王讳胡，及庄王之子名胡，其比众多。
value.en: King Li banned “Hu,” yet Zhuang’s son was Hu—examples abound.
value.literal: Moreover King Li tabooed Hu; and among King Zhuang's sons one was named Hu—their parallels are numerous.

value.zh: 夫类事建议，经有明据，传有徵案，然后进攻退守，万无奔北，垂示百世，永无咎失。
value.en: Advice must rest on canonical proof and commentary precedent—otherwise posterity laughs.
value.literal: When grouping affairs and proposing counsel, the classics have clear proofs and the commentaries verifiable cases—then advancing attack or retreating defense never flees north in defeat; displaying for a hundred generations, never failing or missing.

value.zh: 今应劭虽上尊旧君之名，而下无所断齐，犹归之疑云。
value.en: Ying Shao honors old masters’ names yet sets no clear rule below—it stays muddled.
value.literal: Now although Ying Shao upward honors former lords' names, downward he decides nothing uniform—still it returns to doubtful clouds.

value.zh: 曲礼之篇，疑事无质，观省上下，阙义自证，文辞可为，倡而不法，将来何观？
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette passages he cites prove nothing; pretty words without law teach nothing.
value.literal: The Summary of Etiquette chapter—doubtful matters lack substance; observing above and below, missing righteousness proves itself—literary phrasing may be composed, advocated but not lawful—what will the future behold?

value.zh: 言声一放，犹拾瀋也，过辞在前，悔其何追！”〉
value.en: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉
value.literal: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉

value.zh: 刺史陶謙舉茂才，不應，謙以為輕己，遂見拘執。
value.en: Prefect Tao Qian nominated him for office; when Zhang Zhao declined, Tao felt insulted and jailed him.
value.literal: Inspector Tao Qian nominated him outstanding talent; he did not respond—Qian thought he slighted himself and thereupon had him seized.

value.zh: 昱傾身營救，方以得免。
value.en: Zhao Yu spent himself on bail until Zhang Zhao went free.
value.literal: Yu threw himself into arranging rescue—only then did he obtain release.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，徐方士民多避難揚土，昭皆南渡江。
value.en: Late Han turmoil drove Xu refugees south—Zhang Zhao crossed with them.
value.literal: At the end of Han great chaos arose; gentlemen and commoners of Xu region mostly fled calamity to Yang territory—Zhao all crossed the river south.

value.zh: 孫策創業，命昭為長史、撫軍中郎將，升堂拜母，如比肩之舊，文武之事，一以委昭。
value.en: Sun Ce named him chief clerk and general who pacifies the army, treated him like family before Lady Wu, and handed him every civil and military file.
value.literal: When Sun Ce founded the enterprise he appointed Zhao chief clerk and General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the Army, ascended the hall to bow to his mother as with old peers shoulder to shoulder—civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：策得昭甚悦，谓曰：“吾方有事四方，以士人贤者上，吾於子不得轻矣。”
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Ce rejoiced: I mean to stride the empire—among scholar-advisers I must honor you.
value.literal: [Wu shu] states: Ce gained Zhao and was very pleased, saying to him: I am about to have affairs in the four quarters—with scholar worthies above I cannot treat you lightly.

value.zh: 乃上为校尉，待以师友之礼。〉
value.en: So he raised him to colonel and courted him as mentor.
value.literal: Thereupon he promoted him to colonel and treated him with the ritual of teacher and friend.

value.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，昭欲嘿而不宣則懼有私，宣之則恐非宜，進退不安。
value.en: Northern letters flattered Zhang Zhao alone; silence seemed sneaky, publication awkward—he squirmed either way.
value.literal: Whenever Zhao obtained letters from northern gentlemen-officials they exclusively attributed praise to Zhao; Zhao wished to keep silent and not announce yet feared there was partiality; announcing yet feared it was not appropriate—advancing and retreating were uneasy.

value.zh: 策聞之，歡笑曰："昔管仲相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。
value.en: Sun Ce laughed: Guan Zhong called Huan Gong Father twice—and Huan became hegemon.
value.literal: When Ce heard it he laughed happily and said: Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—first 'Father Zhong,' second 'Father Zhong,' yet Duke Huan became hegemon-in-chief.

value.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎!"，
value.en: Zibu is worthy; if I use him well, the glory is surely mine!
value.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will the merit and fame alone not rest with me!"

value.zh: 譚字子默，弱冠與諸葛恪等為太子四友，從中庶子轉輔正都尉。
value.en: Gu Tan, styled Zimo, was one of Sun Deng's four companions and became aide commandant.
value.literal: Tan courtesy name Zimo—at capping age together with Zhuge Ke and others were heir four friends—from gentleman attendant of heir transferred aide commandant who assists rectitude.

value.zh: 〈陆机为谭传曰：宣太子正位东宫，天子方隆训导之义，妙简俊彦，讲学左右。
value.en: 〈Lu Ji's biography of Gu Tan: when Sun Deng took the eastern palace, the court packed his salon with talent.)
value.literal: 〈Lu Ji for Tan biography states: When Crown Prince came correct to eastern palace—Son of Heaven just then elevated instruction and guidance meaning—subtly selected brilliant talents—studying lecturing left and right.

value.zh: 时四方之杰毕集，太傅诸葛恪等雄奇盖众，而谭以清识绝伦，独见推重。
value.en: Zhuge Ke dominated the heir's court, yet Gu Tan's clarity won highest esteem.
value.literal: At that time four quarters' heroes all gathered—Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke and others heroic strange surpassing host—yet Tan by pure insight unmatched—alone seen pushed weighty.

value.zh: 自太尉范慎、谢景、羊徽之徒，皆以秀称其名，而悉在谭下。〉
value.en: Men like Fan Shen lauded Gu Tan above themselves.〉
value.literal: From Grand Commandant Fan Shen, Xie Jing, Yang Hui's cohort—all by excellence praised their names—yet all ranked below Tan.〉

value.zh: 赤烏中，代恪為左節度。
value.en: In Chiwu he succeeded Zhuge Ke as left quartermaster.
value.literal: In Chiwu replaced Ke as left quartermaster.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：谭初践官府，上疏陈事，权辍食称善，以为过於徐详。
value.en: 〈Wu shu: Sun Quan skipped a meal praising his first memorial.)
value.literal: 〈Wu shu states: Tan first treading official bureau—submitted memorial stating affairs—Quan stopped eating praising good—thought surpassed Xu Xiang.

value.zh: 雅性高亮，不脩意气，或以此望之。
value.en: His lofty cold manner drew resentment.
value.literal: By nature lofty bright—not cultivating temperament—some therefore blamed him.

value.zh: 然权鉴其能，见待甚隆，数蒙赏赐，特见召请。〉
value.en: Sun Quan still favored and enriched him.〉
value.literal: Yet Quan mirrored his ability—treatment very lofty—repeatedly received rewards—specially summoned invited.〉

value.zh: 每省簿書，未嘗下籌，徒屈指心計，盡發疑謬，下吏以此服之。
value.en: He audited ledgers in his head without counting rods and caught every error.
value.literal: Whenever examining registry documents—never lowered counting rods—only bent fingers mental reckoning—fully issuing doubtful errors—subordinate clerks thereby submitted to him.

value.zh: 加奉車都尉。
value.en: He added chief of carriages and cavalry.
value.literal: Added Chief of Carriages and Cavalry Commandant.

value.zh: 薛綜為選曹尚書，固讓譚曰：“譚心精體密，貫道達微，才照人物，德允眾望，誠非愚臣所可越先。”
value.en: Personnel chief Xue Zong ceded the post: Gu Tong exceeds me in every way.
value.literal: Xue Zong was Selection Bureau Secretary—firmly yielding to Tan saying: "Tan mind refined body meticulous—pierces Way reaches subtle—talent illuminates men of affairs—virtue matches multitude hope—truly not what foolish minister can leap ahead."

value.zh: 後遂代綜。
value.en: Gu Tan took personnel.
value.literal: Thereafter succeeded Zong.

value.zh: 虞翻字仲翔，會稽餘姚人也。
value.en: Yu Fan, styled Zhongxiang, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
value.literal: Yu Fan, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻少好学，有高气。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that as a young man Yu Fan loved scholarship and carried himself with uncommon elevation.
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: In youth Fan loved learning and bore himself with lofty pride.

value.zh: 年十二，客有候其兄者，不过翻，翻追与书曰：“仆闻虎魄不取腐芥，磁石不受曲针，过而不存，不亦宜乎！”
value.en: When he was twelve, a visitor called on his brother but snubbed Yu Fan; Fan sent a letter after him: "They say amber ignores rotten mustard and a lodestone spurns a crooked needle—a slight delivered and unnoticed sits ill with neither party."
value.literal: At age twelve a guest came to call on his elder brother but passed by without stopping for Fan; Fan pursued him with a letter saying: "I have heard that amber does not pick up rotten mustard and the lodestone does not take a bent needle; to pass by and pay no heed—is that not fitting!"

value.zh: 客得书奇之，由是见称。〉
value.en: The guest read the note with admiration, and Fan's reputation began from that hour.〉
value.literal: When the guest received the letter he marveled at it, and from this Fan was praised.〉

value.zh: 太守王朗命為功曹。
value.en: The Administrator Wang Lang named him Clerk of Merit.
value.literal: Administrator Wang Lang appointed him Clerk of Merit.

value.zh: 孫策征會稽，翻時遭父喪，衰絰詣府門，朗欲就之，翻乃脫衰入見，勸朗避策。
value.en: While Sun Ce was marching on Kuaiji, Yu Fan was in mourning for his father; he appeared at the yamen gate in sackcloth. Wang Lang meant to comfort him, but Fan stripped the mourning garb, went inside, and urged Lang to withdraw rather than face Ce.
value.literal: Sun Ce campaigned against Kuaiji; Fan was then mourning his father and came to the administrator's gate in mourning dress with hemp cord. Lang wished to approach him, but Fan removed his mourning garments and entered to see him, urging Lang to avoid Ce.

value.zh: 朗不能用。
value.en: Lang would not follow his counsel.
value.literal: Lang could not employ him.

value.zh: 拒戰敗績，亡走浮海。
value.en: He fought and was routed, then fled by ship onto the open sea.
value.literal: He resisted in battle and suffered defeat, then fled and went out to sea.

value.zh: 翻追隨營護，到東部候官，候官長閉城不受，翻往說之，然後見納。
value.en: Fan stayed with the column as escort until they reached Houguan in the eastern circuit; the county magistrate barred the gates until Fan talked him round and won them entry.
value.literal: Fan followed to guard the camp; they reached Houguan in the eastern division. The chief of Houguan closed the city and would not receive them; Fan went and persuaded him, and only then were they admitted.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻始欲送朗到广陵，朗惑王方平记，言“疾来邀我，南岳相求”，故遂南行。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that Fan first meant to see Wang Lang safely to Guangling, "but Lang trusted an inscription attributed to Wang Fangping—Hasten and summon me; the Southern Peak calls—and turned his course southward instead."
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Fan had first wished to escort Lang to Guangling; Lang was misled by Wang Fangping's inscription, which said Come swiftly and invite me; the Southern Marchmount seeks me, "and therefore went south."

value.zh: 既至候官，又欲投交州，翻谏朗曰：“此妄书耳，交州无南岳，安所投乎？”
value.en: At Houguan he planned to bolt for Jiaozhou; Fan warned him: "That text is nonsense—there is no Southern Marchmount in Jiaozhou; what harbor could such a sign point to?"
value.literal: After reaching Houguan he wished again to flee to Jiaozhou. Fan remonstrated with Lang: "This is a false inscription; Jiaozhou has no Southern Marchmount—where would you go?"

value.zh: 乃止。〉
value.en: Lang gave up the idea.
value.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

value.zh: 朗謂翻曰："卿有老母，可以還矣。"
value.en: Lang told him: "You have an old mother at home—you should go back."
value.literal: Lang said to Fan: "You have an aged mother; you may return."

value.zh: 〈翻别传曰：朗使翻见豫章太守华歆，图起义兵。
value.en: 〈Yu Fan's separate biography says Wang Lang dispatched him to Yuzhang's Hua Xin to plan raising loyal troops.
value.literal: 〈The Separate Biography of Fan states: Lang sent Fan to see Administrator Hua Xin of Yuzhang, plotting to raise troops in righteous revolt.

value.zh: 翻未至豫章，闻孙策向会稽，翻乃还。
value.en: Before he reached Yuzhang he learned Sun Ce was bearing down on Kuaiji and wheeled about.
value.literal: Before Fan reached Yuzhang he heard that Sun Ce was heading for Kuaiji, and Fan then returned.

value.zh: 会遭父丧，以臣使有节，不敢过家，星行追朗至候官。
value.en: His father had just died, yet as an accredited envoy he would not detour home; he marched nights until he caught Wang Lang at Houguan.
value.literal: It happened that he was in mourning for his father; as an envoy under orders he dared not pass his home, but traveled by night and overtook Lang at Houguan.

value.zh: 朗遣翻还，然后奔丧。
value.en: Lang released him to return, and only then could Fan observe the funeral rites.
value.literal: Lang sent Fan back, and only then did Fan go to mourn.

value.zh: 而传云孙策之来，翻衰绖诣府门，劝朗避策，则为大异。〉
value.en: The main narrative, however, claims that when Ce approached, Fan appeared at the yamen in mourning bands urging Lang to yield—quite another story.〉
value.literal: Yet the biography says that when Ce came, Fan in mourning dress went to the gate and urged Lang to avoid Ce—this is a great discrepancy.〉

value.zh: 翻既歸，策覆命為功曹，待以交友之禮。
value.en: Once Fan was back, Sun Ce restored him as Clerk of Merit and courted him as an equal.
value.literal: After Fan returned, Ce again appointed him Clerk of Merit and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.

value.zh: 身詣翻第。
value.en: He called at Fan's house himself.
value.literal: He went in person to Fan's residence.

value.zh: 〈江表传曰：策书谓翻曰：“今日之事，当与卿共之，勿谓孙策作郡吏相待也。”〉
value.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan records Ce's letter: "What we face now we shoulder together—do not imagine I would handle you like any county clerk."〉
value.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce wrote to Fan: "Today's affair I must share with you; do not think Sun Ce means to treat you as a mere clerk of the commandery."〉

value.zh: 翻有十一子。
value.en: Yu Fan fathered eleven sons.
value.literal: Fan had eleven sons.

value.zh: 第四子汜最知名，永安初，從選曹朗為散騎中常侍，後為監軍使者，討扶嚴，病卒，
value.en: Fourth-born Si stood tallest—promoted from Selection clerk to mounted attendant, then died leading troops against Fuyan.
value.literal: The fourth son, Si, was most renowned; at the start of Yong'an he went from Gentleman of the Selection Bureau to Regular Mounted Attendant; later he became Military Supervisor Envoy on the campaign against Fuyan and died of illness.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：汜字世洪，生南海，年十六，父卒，还乡里。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu says Si, styled Shihong, was Nanhai-born and came home at sixteen when his father died.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Si, courtesy name Shihong, was born in Nanhai; at sixteen sui his father died and he returned to his native place.

value.zh: 孙綝废幼主，迎立琅邪王休。
value.en: Sun Lin cast the boy emperor aside for Prince Langye's Sun Xiu.
value.literal: Sun Lin deposed the young ruler and welcomed Prince Langye Wang Xiu to succeed.

value.zh: 休未至，綝欲入宫，图为不轨，召百官会议，皆惶怖失色，徒唯唯而已。
value.en: Lin meant to seize the palace before Xiu arrived; the bureaucrats could only nod, pale.
value.literal: Before Xiu arrived Lin wished to enter the palace and plot treason; he summoned the hundred officials to council—all were terrified and bloodless, uttering only yes-yes.

value.zh: 汜对曰：“明公为国伊周，处将相之位，擅废立之威，将上安宗庙，下惠百姓，大小踊跃，自以伊霍复见。
value.en: "Si told Lin he played Yi Yin to the realm—why panic the court by rushing the harem?
value.literal: Si answered: "You, enlightened lord, stand as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou for the state; you hold general and minister rank and wield power to depose and enthrone—you will pacify the ancestral shrines above and bless the hundred surnames below; great and small leap with joy, each imagining Yi Yin and Huo Guang reborn.

value.zh: 今迎王未至，而欲入宫，如是，群下摇荡，众听疑惑，非所以永终忠孝，扬名后世也。”
value.en: Entering the palace early would shake faith and stain his fame."
value.literal: Now the king you welcome has not arrived yet you wish to enter the palace—in this way subordinates waver and the multitude listens in doubt—it is no way to secure loyalty and filial piety forever or lift your name for later ages."

value.zh: 綝不怿，竟立休。
value.en: Lin sulked yet crowned Xiu.
value.literal: Lin was displeased but in the end enthroned Xiu.

value.zh: 休初即位，汜与贺邵、王蕃、薛莹俱为散骑中常侍。
value.en: Xiu kept Si, He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as close attendants.
value.literal: When Xiu first ascended, Si served with He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as Regular Mounted Attendants.

value.zh: 以讨扶严功拜交州刺史、冠军将军、餘姚侯，寻卒。〉
value.en: Fuyan won him Jiaozhou, the Champion baton, and Yuyan marquisate—then death.〉
value.literal: For merit in the Fuyan campaign he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou, Champion General, and Marquis of Yuyao; soon afterward he died.〉

value.zh: 汜弟忠，宜都太守。
value.en: Younger brother Zhong governed Yidu.
value.literal: Si's younger brother Zhong was Administrator of Yidu.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：忠字世方，翻第五子。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu gives Zhong as Fan's fifth son, styled Shifang.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Zhong, courtesy name Shifang, was Fan's fifth son.

value.zh: 贞固幹事，好识人物，造吴郡陆机於童龀之年，称上虞魏迁於无名之初，终皆远致，为著闻之士。
value.en: Zhong spotted Lu Ji as a boy and Wei Qian before fame—both climbed high.
value.literal: Chaste, firm, capable in affairs, skilled at recognizing men—he sought out Lu Ji of Wu commandery while still in childhood and praised Wei Qian of Shangyu before he had a name; both in the end rose far and became scholars of recorded fame.

value.zh: 交同县王岐於孤宦之族，仕进先至宜都太守，忠乃代之。
value.en: He bonded with clerk-born Wang Qi—Qi held Yidu first, Zhong followed.
value.literal: He befriended Wang Qi of the same county from a clan of orphaned clerks; Wang advanced first to Administrator of Yidu, and Zhong succeeded him.

value.zh: 晋征吴，忠与夷道监陆晏、晏弟中夏督景坚守不下，城溃被害。
value.en: Yu Zhong died defending Yidao beside Lu Yan and Lu Jing when Jin breached the walls.
value.literal: When Jin campaigned against Wu, Zhong with Yidao intendant Lu Yan and Yan's younger brother Central Summer Commander Lu Jing held firm and would not yield; when the city broke they were killed.

value.zh: 忠子谭，字思奥。
value.en: His son Tan styled Si'ao.
value.literal: Zhong's son Tan, courtesy name Si'ao.

value.zh: 《晋阳秋》称谭清贞有检操，外如退弱，内坚正有胆幹。
value.en: The Jinyang qiu calls Tan reserved yet steel inside—soft-spoken but unbending.
value.literal: The Jinyang qiu praises Tan as chaste and restrained with disciplined integrity—outwardly seeming yielding and weak, inwardly firm, upright, and bold in capacity.

value.zh: 仕晋，历位内外，终於卫将军，追赠侍中左光禄大夫，开府仪同三司。〉
value.en: Under Jin he reached Defender-in-Chief and won posthumous ministerial glory.〉
value.literal: He served Jin, rose through inner and outer posts, ending as Defender-in-Chief—posthumously honored Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee with Office Equal to the Three Dukes.〉

value.zh: 聳，越騎校尉。
value.en: Yu Song served as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
value.literal: Song was Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 累遷廷尉，湘東、河間太守；
value.en: He rose to Commandant of Justice and prefect of Xiangdong and Hejian;
value.literal: He was promoted in stages to Commandant of Justice, Administrator of Xiangdong and Hejian;

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：耸字世龙，翻第六子也。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu names Song as Fan's sixth son, styled Shilong.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Song, courtesy name Shilong, was Fan's sixth son.

value.zh: 清虚无欲，进退以礼，在吴历清官，入晋，除河间相，王素闻耸名，厚敬礼之。
value.en: Ascetic and punctilious in Wu, he became Hejian chancellor under Jin; Prince Su honored his reputation.
value.literal: Clear, empty of desire, advancing and retreating by ritual—in Wu he passed through pure offices; entering Jin he was appointed Chancellor of Hejian; Prince Su long hearing Song's name treated him with thick courtesy and respect.

value.zh: 耸抽引人物，务在幽隐孤陋之中。
value.en: He insisted on lifting talent from hedgerows and hovels.
value.literal: Song drew forth men of affairs, striving for those hidden in obscurity, orphaned and lowly.

value.zh: 时王岐难耸，以高士所达，必合秀异，耸书与族子察曰：“世之取士，曾不招未齿於丘园，索良才於总猥，所誉依已成，所毁依已败，此吾所以叹息也。”
value.en: "Wang Qi argued great names imply genius; Song answered his kinsman Cha that patronage chases winners and shuns unknowns—a vice worth mourning."
value.literal: At the time Wang Qi challenged Song: men of lofty repute reach only the outstandingly gifted; Song wrote his clansman Cha: "This age's recruitment never summons the toothless recluse from grove and garden nor seeks fine talent from the crude crowd; praise follows what is already made, slander tracks what is already ruined—that is why I sigh."

value.zh: 耸疾俗丧祭无度，弟昺卒，祭以少牢，酒饭而已，当时族党并遵行之。〉
value.en: He trimmed funeral feasts to wine and grain when Bing died, and kin copied him.〉
value.literal: Song loathed vulgar excess in mourning sacrifices; when younger brother Bing died he offered only the lesser beast sacrifice—wine and rice—and kinsmen alike followed the rule.〉

value.zh: 昺，廷尉尚書，濟陰太守。
value.en: Bing rose to ministerial rank and governed Jiyin.
value.literal: Bing was Minister of Justice and Minister over the Masses, Administrator of Jiyin.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昺字世文，翻第八子也。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu records Bing, Fan's eighth son, styled Shiwen.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Bing, courtesy name Shiwen, was Fan's eighth son.

value.zh: 少有倜傥之志，仕吴黄门郎，以捷对见异，超拜尚书侍中。
value.en: Wu valued his wit at the Yellow Gates and jumped him to palace minister.
value.literal: In youth he cherished a free hero's ambition; serving Wu as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates he was singled out for quick repartee and vaulted to Palace Attendant Minister.

value.zh: 晋军来伐，遣昺持节都督武昌已上诸军事，昺先上还节盖印绶，然后归顺。
value.en: Facing invasion Bing surrendered credentials above Wuchang before yielding.
value.literal: When Jin's army came to strike he dispatched Bing with tally as Area Commander-in-Chief for all military affairs from Wuchang upward; Bing first returned tally, canopy, seals and ribbons, then submitted.

value.zh: 在济阴，抑强扶弱，甚著威风。〉
value.en: At Jiyin he humbled bullies and shielded commoners—justice visible on the street.〉
value.literal: In Jiyin he checked the mighty and aided the weak—his martial awe stood renowned.〉

value.zh: 王蕃字永元，廬江人也。
value.en: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, came from Lujiang commandery.
value.literal: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, was a man of Lujiang.

value.zh: 博覽多聞，兼通術藝。
value.en: He was widely read and well informed, and equally at home with astronomy, mathematics, and the technical arts.
value.literal: He read widely and heard much, and was also versed in technical arts.

value.zh: 始為尚書郎，去官。
value.en: He began as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat, then resigned his post.
value.literal: At first he was gentleman of the masters of writing, then left office.

value.zh: 孫休即位，與賀邵、薛瑩、虞汜俱為散騎中常侍，皆加駙馬都尉。
value.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Wang Fan, He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si were all named attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, each with the additional title chief commandant of carriage escort.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.

value.zh: 時論清之。
value.en: Public opinion ranked them among the court's clearest spirits.
value.literal: Contemporary opinion deemed them pure.

value.zh: 遣使至蜀，蜀人稱焉，還為夏口監軍。
value.en: Sent on embassy to Shu, he won high praise there; on his return he was named supervisor of the army at Xiakou.
value.literal: He was sent as envoy to Shu; the people of Shu praised him, and on return he became supervisor of the army at Xiakou.

value.zh: 書奏，皓深恨之。
value.en: Sun Hao read the memorial and nursed a deep grudge.
value.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Hao deeply hated him.

value.zh: 邵奉公貞正，親近所憚。
value.en: He Shao was incorrupt and upright—the emperor's favorites feared him.
value.literal: Shao served the public with integrity and uprightness; those intimate with the ruler feared him.

value.zh: 乃共譖邵與樓玄謗毀國事，俱被詰責。
value.en: They framed He Shao and Lou Xuan for defaming the state; both were censured.
value.literal: Thereupon they jointly slandered Shao and Lou Xuan as slandering and ruining state affairs; both received edict interrogation and blame.

value.zh: 玄見送南州，邵原復職。
value.en: Lou Xuan went south while He Shao was briefly restored.
value.literal: Xuan was seen off to the southern province; Shao was originally restored to office.

value.zh: 後邵中惡風，口不能言，去職數月，皓疑其托疾，收付酒藏，掠考千所，邵卒無一語，竟見殺害，家屬徙臨海。
value.en: He Shao fell mute with a stroke; Sun Hao called it shamming, jailed him in the wine office, tortured him endlessly—He never spoke and was murdered; his kin were banished to Linhai.
value.literal: Afterward Shao was struck by evil wind and could not speak; he left office several months; Hao suspected he feigned illness, seized him and handed him to the wine bureau, tortured and examined at a thousand places—Shao to the end had not one word, and in the end was killed; family dependants were moved to Linhai.

value.zh: 並下詔誅玄子孫，是歲天冊元年也，邵年四十九。
value.en: The same year Sun Hao ordered Lou Xuan's descendants executed; it was the first year of Tiance; He Shao was forty-nine.
value.literal: At the same time an edict went down to execute Xuan's sons and grandsons; it was the first year of the Tiance era; Shao was forty-nine years old.

value.zh: 〈邵子循，字彦先。
value.en: 〈His son He Xun, courtesy name Yanxian,
value.literal: 〈Shao's son Xun, courtesy name Yanxian.

value.zh: 虞预晋书曰：循丁家祸，流放海滨，吴平，还乡里。
value.en: Yu Yu's Jin History says He Xun suffered family ruin, was exiled to the coast, and returned home when Wu fell.
value.literal: Yu Yu's Jin shu states: Xun suffered family disaster, was banished to the sea's edge; when Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.

value.zh: 节操高厉，童齔不群，言行举动，必以礼让。
value.en: High-minded from childhood, he stood apart from other boys and was always courteous in word and deed.
value.literal: His integrity was lofty and stern; from childhood he stood apart from others, and in speech and conduct he always acted with ritual courtesy.

value.zh: 好学博闻，尤善三礼。
value.en: He loved books and excelled in the three ritual classics.
value.literal: He loved learning and read widely, especially skilled in the three ritual canons.

value.zh: 举秀子，除阳羡、武康令。
value.en: Recommended as a flourishing talent, he became magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.
value.literal: Recommended as flourishing talent, he was appointed magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.

value.zh: 顾荣、陆机、陆云表荐循曰：“伏见吴兴武康令贺循德量邃茂，才鉴清远，服膺道素，风操凝峻，历践三城，刑政肃穆，守职下县，编名凡萃，出自新邦，朝无知己，恪居遐外，志不自营，年时倏忽，而邈无阶绪，实州党愚智所为怅然。
value.en: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun jointly memorialized: "We humbly see that He Xun of Wukang combines depth of character with clarity of judgment, lives by the plain Way, and has governed three counties with a stern hand. A man of a newly conquered land without patrons at court, he languishes in a minor post while years slip away—the whole province grieves to see talent wasted.
value.literal: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun submitted a memorial recommending Xun, saying: We humbly see that He Xun, magistrate of Wukang in Wuxing, has deep and abundant virtue and measure, talent and insight clear and far, embraces the plain of the Way, conduct and integrity stern and lofty; he has passed through three cities in office, punishments and government solemn, guarding duty in a lower county, his name listed among the common mass, coming from a new state, the court without one who knows him, respectfully dwelling far outside, his intent not self-seeking, years and seasons suddenly passing, yet far without ladder or thread—truly what the foolish and wise of the province together feel regret about.

value.zh: 臣等并以凡才，累授饰进，被服恩泽，忝豫朝末，知良士后时，而守局无言，惧有蔽贤之咎，是以不胜愚管，谨冒死表闻。”
value.en: We are mediocre men already favored at court; to stay silent while a worthy languishes would be to hide talent from you—we therefore risk death to speak."
value.literal: We your servants are all with ordinary talent, repeatedly receiving advancement in ornament, clothed in favor and grace, shamefully placed at the court's end; knowing a good gentleman is behind the times yet guarding our posts without speech, we fear the fault of concealing the worthy—therefore, unable to bear our foolish tubes, we respectfully risk death to set forth and be heard.

value.zh: 久之，召为太子舍人。
value.en: After long delay he was named attendant to the heir apparent.
value.literal: After a long time he was summoned to be attendant to the heir apparent.

value.zh: 石冰破扬州，循亦合众，事平，杜门不出。
value.en: When Shi Bing ravaged Yangzhou, He Xun raised troops; when peace returned he shut his gates and would not show himself.
value.literal: When Shi Bing broke Yangzhou, Xun also gathered a host; when the affair was settled, he closed his door and did not go out.

value.zh: 陈敏作乱，以循为丹杨内史，循称疾固辞，敏不敢逼。
value.en: Chen Min tried to name him interior administrator of Danyang; He Xun pleaded illness and Chen Min dared not press him.
value.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, he appointed Xun as interior administrator of Danyang; Xun claimed illness and firmly declined—Min did not dare force him.

value.zh: 于时江东豪右无不受敏爵位，惟循与同郡硃诞不挂贼网。
value.en: While every great clan in Jiangdong took Chen Min's commissions, only He Xun and his townsman Zhu Dan refused the rebel's snare.
value.literal: At that time among the powerful families east of the Yangzi none did not accept titles from Min—only Xun together with Zhu Dan of his commandery did not hang in the rebel's net.

value.zh: 后除吴国内史，不就。
value.en: He was later offered interior administrator of Wu but declined.
value.literal: Afterward he was appointed interior administrator of Wu commandery but did not take up the post.

value.zh: 元皇帝为镇东将军，请循为军司马，帝为晋王，以循为中书令，固让不受，转太常，领太子太傅。
value.en: When Sima Rui was general who guards the east he asked He Xun to be his army marshal; as Prince of Jin he offered the secretariat—He Xun refused—and made him grand master of ceremonies and grand tutor to the heir apparent instead.
value.literal: When Emperor Yuan was general who guards the east, he requested Xun as army marshal; when the Prince became Prince of Jin, he made Xun director of the secretariat—he firmly declined and would not accept, was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent.

value.zh: 时朝廷初建，动有疑议，宗庙制度皆循所定，朝野谘询，为一时儒宗。
value.en: In the new Jin court he settled every disputed ritual and became the age's leading Confucian authority.
value.literal: At that time the court was newly established; whenever there was doubt in discussion, the rites of the ancestral temple were all what Xun settled; court and wild consulted him—he was the Confucian leader of the age.

value.zh: 年六十，太兴二年卒。
value.en: He died at sixty in the second year of Taixing (319).
value.literal: At age sixty he died in the second year of Taixing.

value.zh: 追赠司空，谥曰穆。
value.en: He was posthumously named minister of works with the posthumous epithet Mu.
value.literal: Posthumously he was honored as minister of works, posthumous name Mu.

value.zh: 循诸所著论，并传於世。
value.en: His essays survive in his collected works.
value.literal: The various treatises Xun wrote were all transmitted in the world.

value.zh: 子隰，临海太守。〉
value.en: His son He Xi became grand administrator of Linhai.
value.literal: His son Xi was grand administrator of Linhai.

value.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京師，擊長沙王乂。
value.en: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Hui of Jin's reign, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, ordered Lu Ji to march on the capital and strike the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.
value.literal: In the second year of Tai'an of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, sent Lu Ji at the head of an army toward the capital to attack the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.

value.zh: 軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅。
value.en: The army had barely moved when the command pennant pole broke; shortly afterward the force was routed and Lu Ji was put to death.
value.literal: As soon as the army set out the command pennant staff snapped; soon afterward they were defeated and Ji was executed.

value.zh: 穎尋奔潰，卒賜死。
value.en: Ying soon fled in defeat and was eventually compelled to commit suicide.
value.literal: Ying soon fled in rout and in the end was ordered to take his own life.

value.zh: 初，河間王顒謀先誅長沙，廢太子，立穎。
value.en: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had planned to kill the Prince of Changsha first, depose the crown prince, and set up Ying in his place.
value.literal: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had plotted first to kill the Prince of Changsha, depose the heir, and install Ying.

value.zh: 長沙知之，誅其黨卞粹等，故穎來伐。
value.en: The Prince of Changsha uncovered the plot and executed Yong's allies Bian Cui and the rest, which brought Ying's invasion.
value.literal: The Prince of Changsha learned of it and executed his partisans Bian Cui and others; therefore Ying came to attack.

value.zh: 機又以穎得遐邇心，將為漢之代王，遂委質於穎，為犯從之將。
value.en: Lu Ji likewise believed Ying had won universal support and would replace the Han house as king; he therefore pledged himself to Ying and served as a general in the rebel host.
value.literal: Ji also thought that because Ying had won the hearts of near and far he would become the Han dynasty's replacement king, and therefore submitted to Ying and served as a general who followed the rebel cause.

value.zh: 此皆姦謀之罰，木不曲直也。
value.en: All of this fell under the penalty for treacherous designs—wood failing to be straight or bent.
value.literal: All these were punishments for treacherous plots—wood not straight or bent.

value.zh: 孝建三年，卒，時年七十三。
value.en: In the third year of Xiaojian (456) he died at the age of seventy-three.
value.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian (456), he died, aged seventy-three.

value.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、特進，金紫光祿大夫如故。
value.en: He was posthumously granted Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Special Advancement, while retaining his rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
value.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Special Advancement, with Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon as before.

value.zh: 諡曰憲子。
value.en: His posthumous title was Xianzi, "The Principled."
value.literal: His posthumous title was Xianzi (The Principled).

value.zh: 延之與陳郡謝靈運俱以詞彩齊名，自潘岳、陸機之後，文士莫及也，江左稱顏、謝焉。
value.en: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen were equally famed for literary brilliance; since Pan Yue and Lu Ji, no writer had matched them—the south spoke of Yan and Xie.
value.literal: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery were both famed for equal brilliance in letters; since Pan Yue and Lu Ji, no man of letters could match them—the Eastern Jin called them Yan and Xie.

value.zh: 所著並傳於世。
value.en: His writings have all been handed down to posterity.
value.literal: All that he wrote has been handed down in the world.

value.zh: 列傳第四十一 劉秀之 顧琛 顧覬之
value.en: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, and Gu Jizhi
value.literal: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi

value.zh: 顧覬之，字偉仁，吳郡吳人也。
value.en: Gu Jizhi, whose style was Weiren, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
value.literal: Gu Jizhi, style name Weiren, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.

value.zh: 高祖謙，字公讓，晉平原內史陸機姊夫。
value.en: His great-grandfather Qian, whose style was Gongrang, was the brother-in-law of Lu Ji, Interior Governor of Pingyuan under Jin.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Qian, style name Gongrang, was brother-in-law to Lu Ji, Jin Interior Governor of Pingyuan.

value.zh: 祖崇，大司農。
value.en: His grandfather Chong had served as Director of the Grand Granary.
value.literal: His grandfather Chong was Director of the Grand Granary.

value.zh: 父黃老，司徒左西掾。
value.en: His father Huanglao had served as Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.
value.literal: His father Huanglao was Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.

value.zh: 覬之初為郡主簿。
value.en: Jizhi began his career as chief clerk of his commandery.
value.literal: Jizhi first served as commandery chief clerk.

value.zh: 謝晦為荊州，以為南蠻功曹，仍為晦衛軍參軍。
value.en: When Xie Hui was posted to Jingzhou, he appointed Jizhi Merit Officer for the Southern Man and then staff officer on Hui's Guard Army.
value.literal: When Xie Hui held Jingzhou, he made him Merit Officer for the Southern Man and then staff officer on Hui's Guard Army.

value.zh: 晦愛其雅素，深相知待。
value.en: Hui admired his refined simplicity and treated him with deep trust and regard.
value.literal: Hui loved his refined simplicity and treated him with deep mutual regard.

value.zh: 王弘辟為揚州主簿，仍為弘衛軍參軍，鹽官令，衡陽王義季右軍主簿，尚書都官郎，護軍司馬。
value.en: Wang Hong recruited him as chief clerk of Yangzhou, then as staff officer on Hong's Guard Army, magistrate of Yanguan, Right Army chief clerk to Prince Yiji of Hengyang, an officer in the Secretariat's capital-crimes section, and Protecting Army marshal.
value.literal: Wang Hong recruited him as Yangzhou chief clerk, then as Hong's Guard Army staff officer, magistrate of Yanguan, Right Army chief clerk to Prince of Hengyang Yiji, Secretariat Officer in the Capital Crimes section, and Protecting Army marshal.

value.zh: 時大將軍彭城王義康秉權，殷、劉之隙已著，覬之不欲與殷景仁久接事，乃辭腳疾自免歸。
value.en: At the time Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held power, and the rift between Yin Jingren and Liu Yilong was already open. Jizhi did not wish to serve alongside Yin Jingren and pleaded a foot ailment to resign and return home.
value.literal: At the time the Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, held power; the rift between Yin and Liu was already manifest; Jizhi did not wish to serve long with Yin Jingren and so pleaded foot ailment to resign and return home.

value.zh: 在家每夜常于床上行腳，家人竊異之，而莫曉其意。
value.en: At home he would walk about on his bed each night. His family found this strange but none understood his purpose.
value.literal: At home each night he would often walk his feet upon the bed; the household privately found it strange but none understood his intent.

value.zh: 後義康徙廢，朝廷多以異同受禍。
value.en: Later, when Yikang was demoted and disgraced, many at court suffered ruin for their political affiliations.
value.literal: Later Yikang was demoted and disgraced; many at court suffered calamity for their affiliations.

value.zh: 復為東遷、山陰令。
value.en: He again served as magistrate of Dongqian and Shanyin in succession.
value.literal: He again served as magistrate of Dongqian and Shanyin.

value.zh: 山陰民戶三萬，海內劇邑，前後官長，晝夜不得休，事猶不舉。
value.en: Shanyin had thirty thousand households and was among the most demanding counties in the realm. Successive magistrates worked day and night without rest, yet still could not keep up with their duties.
value.literal: Shanyin had thirty thousand households, a commandery of the greatest difficulty within the realm; successive magistrates could not rest day or night, yet affairs still went unaccomplished.

value.zh: 覬之理繁以約，縣用無事，晝日垂簾，門階閑寂。
value.en: Jizhi governed complexity through simplicity. The county ran without incident; by day he let the curtain hang down, and his gate and courtyard stood quiet and still.
value.literal: Jizhi governed complexity through simplicity; the county had no troubles; by day he let the curtain hang and the gate and steps were quiet and still.

value.zh: 自宋世為山陰，務簡而績修，莫能尚也。
value.en: From the Song period onward, no magistrate of Shanyin had matched his combination of simple administration and well-ordered achievement.
value.literal: From the Song era as magistrate of Shanyin, his affairs were simple yet his achievements well ordered—none could surpass him.

value.zh: 還為揚州治中從事史，廣陵王誕、廬陵王紹北中郎左司馬，揚州別駕從事史，尚書吏部郎。
value.en: He returned to serve as Senior Clerk of Yangzhou, Northern Central Left Staff Officer to Princes Dan of Guangling and Shao of Luling, Vice Director of Yangzhou, and an officer in the Secretariat's civil-service section.
value.literal: He returned as Yangzhou Senior Clerk, Northern Central Left Staff Officer to Princes of Guangling Dan and of Luling Shao, Yangzhou Vice Director, and Secretariat Officer in the Civil Service section.

value.zh: 嘗于太祖坐論江左人物，言及顧榮，袁淑謂覬之曰：「卿南人怯懦，豈辦作賊。」
value.en: Once, at a gathering of Taizu discussing figures of the Jiang left, Gu Rong's name came up. Yuan Shu said to Jizhi, "You southerners are timid and weak—how could you ever manage to be rebels?"
value.literal: Once at a gathering of Taizu discussing figures of the Jiang left, when Gu Rong was mentioned Yuan Shu said to Jizhi: "You southerners are timid and weak—how could you manage to be rebels?"

value.zh: 覬之正色曰：「卿乃複以忠義笑人！」
value.en: Jizhi replied with a stern face, "You would mock a man for his loyalty and righteousness!"
value.literal: Jizhi with stern countenance said: "You would mock a man for his loyalty and righteousness!"

value.zh: 淑有愧色。
value.en: Shu looked ashamed.
value.literal: Shu showed a look of shame.

value.zh: 對曰：子可謂扶繩而辨，循刻而議。
value.en: He replied: You may be said to argue by holding the rope of the argument and to debate by following the sundial's shadow—your reasoning is exacting indeed.
value.literal: The reply came: You may be said to argue by holding a rope and to debate by following a marking on the sundial.

value.zh: 若乃宣攝有方，豈非吉運所屬；
value.en: As for regulating and governing with proper method—is that not the province of fortunate destiny?
value.literal: As for regulating and governing with proper method—is that not what fortunate destiny belongs to?

value.zh: 將迎有會，實亦凶數自挻。
value.en: That meeting has its occasion is true; yet ill-fated numbers also extend themselves of their own accord.
value.literal: That meeting has its occasion is true; yet ill-fated numbers also extend themselves.

value.zh: 若夫陽施陰德，長世遐年，揆厥所原，孰往非命。
value.en: As for active benevolence and hidden virtue, long generations and distant years—when one traces them to their origin, where does anything go that is not fate?
value.literal: As for yang-bestowal and yin-virtue, long generations and distant years—when one traces them to their origin, where does anything go that is not fate?

value.zh: 研復來旨，讎校往說，起予惟商，未識所異。
value.en: I have studied your latest meaning and collated it with earlier discourse. You enlighten me—I can discuss with you, yet I do not see where we differ.
value.literal: I have studied your latest meaning and collated it with earlier discourse; you enlighten me—I can discuss with you, yet I do not see where we differ.

value.zh: 資生稟運，參差萬殊，逆順吉凶，理數不一。
value.en: The endowment of life and received fortune vary among ten thousand differences; rebellion and obedience, good and ill, follow principles and numbers that are not one.
value.literal: The endowment of life and received fortune vary among ten thousand differences; rebellion and obedience, good and ill, follow principles and numbers that are not one.

value.zh: 原夫餐椒非養生之術，咀劍豈衛性之經。
value.en: For eating pepper is not a method of nourishing life, and chewing swords is hardly a canon for guarding one's nature.
value.literal: For eating pepper is not a method of nourishing life, and chewing swords is hardly a canon for guarding one's nature.

value.zh: 命之所延，人肉其骨，而含嚼膏粱，時或嬰患。
value.en: Where fate extends life, one may eat human flesh to the bone—yet those who chew rich grains still sometimes contract illness.
value.literal: Where fate extends life, one eats human flesh to the bone—yet those who chew rich grains still sometimes contract illness.

value.zh: 深澗乖徼寵之津，空谷絕探榮之轍，運之所集，物稊其枯，而俯仰竿牘，終然離沮。
value.en: Deep ravines lack paths to favor; empty valleys cut off tracks to glory—where fortune gathers, things wither to dryness, while those who bow and rise with brush and document still end in separation and dejection.
value.literal: Deep ravines miss the ford of favor; empty valleys cut off tracks of seeking glory—where fortune gathers, things wither to dryness, while those who bow and rise with brush and document still end in separation and dejection.

value.zh: 爾乃蹻、蹠橫行；
value.en: Then Bo Yi and Robber Zhi go unrestrained;
value.literal: Then Bo Yi and Robber Zhi go unrestrained;

value.zh: 曾、原窘步。
value.en: Zeng Shen and Yan Yuan walk in distress.
value.literal: Zeng Shen and Yan Yuan walk in distress.

value.zh: 湯、周延世，詡、邑絕緒。
value.en: Tang and Zhou extended their lines through generations; Xu You and Boyi ended without posterity.
value.literal: Tang and Zhou extended their generations; Xu and Yi ended their lines.

value.zh: 吉凶征應，糾纆若茲。
value.en: The omens of good and ill fortune correspond, tangled together thus.
value.literal: The omens of good and ill correspond, tangled together thus.

value.zh: 畢萬保軀，宓賤喪領，梁野之言，豈不或妄。
value.en: Bi Wan preserved his body, Mi Zijian lost his head—are Liang Yi's words not perhaps mistaken?
value.literal: Bi Wan preserved his body, Mi Zijian lost his head—are Liang Yi's words not perhaps mistaken?

value.zh: 谷南、魯北，甘此促生；
value.en: South of the valley, north of Lu—they willingly accept this shortened span of life;
value.literal: South of the valley, north of Lu—they willingly accept this shortened life;

value.zh: 彭翁、竇叟，將以何術。
value.en: Old Peng and Old Dou—by what arts did they do it?
value.literal: Old Peng, Old Dou—by what arts?

value.zh: 晉平、趙敬，淫放已該；
value.en: Duke Ping of Jin and King Jing of Zhao were licentious and dissolute to the full;
value.literal: Duke Ping of Jin and King Jing of Zhao—licentious and dissolute, already complete;

value.zh: 漢主、魏相，奚獨傷夭。
value.en: The Han emperor and the Wei minister—why did they alone die young?
value.literal: The Han lord and the Wei minister—why alone die young?

value.zh: 同異若斯，是非孰正。
value.en: Similarities and differences like these—which view is right and which wrong?
value.literal: Similarities and differences like these—which is right and which wrong?

value.zh: 至如雷濱凝分，挫志遠圖；
value.en: As when at Lei Ford the streams congealed and parted, frustrating ambitions for distant achievement;
value.literal: As when at Lei Ford the streams congealed and parted, frustrating ambitions for distant achievement;

value.zh: 棘津陰拱，振功高世。
value.en: while at Jiji Ford one waited in hidden stillness and shook the age with lofty merit.
value.literal: while at Jiji Ford one waited in hidden stillness and shook the age with lofty merit.

value.zh: 樊生沖矯，鐫旌善之文，華子高抗，銘懲非之策，皆士衡所雲「同川而異歸」者也。
value.en: Fan Sheng strove upward and engraved words praising the good; Hua Zi stood high in opposition and inscribed policies warning against evil—all examples of what Lu Ji called "the same stream yet different destinations."
value.literal: Fan Sheng strove upward and engraved words praising the good; Hua Zi stood high in opposition and inscribed policies warning against evil—all examples of what Lu Ji called "the same stream yet different destinations."

value.zh: 殊塗均致，實繁有征。
value.en: Different paths reach the same end—instances of this are indeed numerous and verified.
value.literal: Different paths reach the same end—instances of this are indeed numerous and verified.

value.zh: 即理易推，在言可略。
value.en: Following from principle one can easily infer; in words it may be brief.
value.literal: Following from principle one can easily infer; in words it may be brief.

value.zh: 昔兩都全盛，六合殷昌，霧集貴寵之閭，雲動權豪之術，鈞貿貽談，豈唯陳、張而已。
value.en: In former days when both capitals were in full splendor and the realm prospered, mist gathered in lanes of noble favor and clouds stirred in wards of powerful magnates—tales of equal standing were handed down; was it only Chen Ping and Zhang Liang?
value.literal: In former days when both capitals were in full splendor and the realm prospered, mist gathered in lanes of noble favor and clouds stirred in wards of powerful magnates—tales of equal price in trade were handed down; was it only Chen and Zhang?

value.zh: 觀夫二子，才未越眾，而此以藉榮揮價，彼獨擯景淪聲，通否之運，斷可知矣。
value.en: Considering these two men, their talent did not surpass the multitude, yet one rode borrowed glory to raise his price while the other alone was cast into shadow and sank in repute—the fortune of passage or obstruction can clearly be known.
value.literal: Considering these two men, their talent did not surpass the multitude, yet one rode borrowed glory to raise his price while the other alone was cast into shadow and sank in repute—the fortune of passage or obstruction can clearly be known.

value.zh: 嚴、辛不安時任命，而委罪亮直，亦地脈之徒歟。
value.en: Yan Jun and Xin Ping did not rest content with their allotted times and appointments, yet blamed the straight and bright—is this also the cohort of those who talk of underground veins?
value.literal: Yan and Xin did not rest content with their allotted times and appointments, yet blamed the straight and bright—is this also the cohort of those who talk of underground veins?

value.zh: 若神仙所序，顯明修習，齊強燕平，厥驗未著，李覃董芬，其效安在。
value.en: As for what immortals set forth and bright cultivation—Qi was strong, Yan was pacified, yet their verification did not appear; Li Tan and Dong Fen—where are their effects?
value.literal: As for what immortals set forth and bright cultivation—Qi was strong, Yan was pacified, yet their verification did not appear; Li Tan and Dong Fen—where are their effects?

value.zh: 喬、松之侶，雲飛天居，夷、列之徒，風行水息，良由理數懸挺，實乃鐘茲景命。
value.en: Companions of Wang Qiao and Chi Songzi soar through clouds and dwell in heaven; followers of Boyi and Liezi move with the wind and rest upon the water—truly because principle and number stand far apart, they in fact received this splendid destiny.
value.literal: Companions of Qiao and Song soar through clouds and dwell in heaven; followers of Boyi and Liezi move with the wind and rest upon the water—truly because principle and number stand far apart, they in fact received this splendid destiny.

value.zh: 天竺遺文，星華方策，因造前定，果報指期，貧豪莫差，修夭無爽，有允瑣辭，無愆鄙說，統而言之，孰往非命。
value.en: India's transmitted texts and the star-flowered cubic charts establish prior determination; karmic retribution points to its term; poor and great are not differentiated, long life and early death are not in error; there are trustworthy petty phrases and no fault in humble discourse—unified in speech, where does anything go that is not fate?
value.literal: India's transmitted texts and the star-flowered cubic charts establish prior determination; karmic retribution points to its term; poor and great are not differentiated, long life and early death are not in error; there are trustworthy petty phrases and no fault in humble discourse—unified in speech, where does anything go that is not fate?

value.zh: 冥期前定，各從所歸，善惡無所矯其趨，愚智焉能殊其理。
value.en: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course—how can fool and sage differ in principle?
value.literal: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course, fool and sage—how can they differ in principle?

value.zh: 若乃得議其工，失嗤其拙，操之則栗，舍之則悲，斯固染情於近累，豈不貽誚於通識。
value.en: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?
value.literal: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?

value.zh: 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔
value.en: Biography 46: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian
value.literal: Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian

value.zh: 史臣曰：吳漢平蜀，城內流血沾踝，而其後無聞於漢；
value.en: The historian says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city soaked to the ankles, yet afterward nothing is heard of him in Han;
value.literal: The historian says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city soaked to the ankles, yet afterward nothing is heard of him in Han;

value.zh: 陸抗定西陵，步氏禍及嬰孩，而機、雲為戮上國。
value.en: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Lu Ji and Lu Yun were executed in the upper state.
value.literal: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Ji and Yun were executed in the upper state.

value.zh: 劉勔克壽春，士民無遺芻委粒之歎；
value.en: When Liu Mian took Shouyang, soldiers and civilians had no lament over lost fodder and scattered grain;
value.literal: When Liu Mian took Shouyang, soldiers and civilians had no lament over lost fodder and scattered grain;

value.zh: 莫不扶老攜幼，歌唱而出重圍，美矣！
value.en: all without exception supported the old and led the young, singing as they came out of the heavy encirclement—how beautiful!
value.literal: all without exception supported the old and led the young, singing as they came out of the heavy encirclement—how beautiful!

value.zh: 南安王楨，皇興二年封，加征南大將軍、中都大官，尋遷內都大官。
value.en: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in Huangxing year 2, made Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon moved to the inner directorate.
value.literal: Zhen, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing, appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, and soon transferred to Director of the Inner Palace within the capital.

value.zh: 高祖即位，除涼州鎮都大將。
value.en: At Gaozu's accession he was made commander of Liangzhou Garrison.
value.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Grand General of Liangzhou Garrison.

value.zh: 尋以綏撫有能，加都督西戎諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護西域校尉、儀同三司、涼州刺史。
value.en: Soon, for skill in pacification, he was added commander of Western Rong armies, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Liangzhou.
value.literal: Soon, for able pacification, he was added commander of all military affairs of the Western Rong, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Protector-General of the Western Regions, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Liangzhou.

value.zh: 徵為內都大官，出為使持節、侍中、本將軍、開府、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。
value.en: He was recalled to the inner directorate, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff and Palace Attendant with his former rank, an open office, command of Chang'an Garrison, and the Yongzhou inspectorate.
value.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Inner Palace within the capital, then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, his former rank, with an open office, Grand General of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

value.zh: 楨性忠謹，事母以孝聞，賜帛千匹以褒之。
value.en: Zhen was loyal and careful, famed for filial service to his mother; the court gave him a thousand bolts of silk in praise.
value.literal: Zhen was by nature loyal and careful; he served his mother with a fame for filial piety and was rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk in praise.

value.zh: 熙既蕃王之貴，加有文學，好奇愛異，交結偉俊，風氣甚高，名美當世，先達後進，多造其門。
value.en: A frontier prince and a man of letters, he sought out brilliant company; the age praised him, and many came to his door.
value.literal: Xi, being noble among the frontier princes, moreover had literature; he loved the strange and cherished the different, formed ties with great and handsome men, his air very lofty, his name beautiful in the age—elders before and juniors after, many came to his gate.

value.zh: 始熙之鎮鄴也，知友才學之士袁翻、李琰、李神儁、王誦兄弟、裴敬憲等咸餞於河梁，賦詩告別。
value.en: When he left for Ye, Yuan Fan, Li Shenjun, the Wang brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others saw him off at River Bridge with poems.
value.literal: When Xi first went to govern Ye, talented literary men Yuan Fan, Li Yan, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others all saw him off at River Bridge, composing poems in farewell.

value.zh: 及熙將死，復與知故書曰：「吾與弟並蒙皇太后知遇，兄據大州，弟則入侍，殷勤言色，恩同慈母。
value.en: Before death he wrote to friends: "My brother and I were cherished by the Empress Dowager—he in a great province, I at court—treated like sons.
value.literal: When Xi was about to die he again wrote to old friends: "I and my younger brother both received the Empress Dowager's knowing encounter; elder brother held a great province, younger brother then entered attendance—earnest words and color, grace like a loving mother.

value.zh: 今皇太后見廢北宮，太傅清河王橫受屠酷，主上幼年，獨在前殿。
value.en: Now she is confined in the North Palace, Prince Yi was butchered, and the boy emperor sits alone.
value.literal: Now the Empress Dowager is deposed in the North Palace; the Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe was slaughtered across; the lord is young, alone in the front hall.

value.zh: 君親如此，無以自安，故率兵民建大義於天下。
value.en: I could not rest; I raised arms in the name of righteousness.
value.literal: Lord and kin thus—I cannot be at peace; therefore I lead soldiers and people to raise great righteousness under Heaven.

value.zh: 但智力淺短，旋見囚執，上慚朝廷，下愧相知。
value.en: My wits were short; I was seized at once—shame to the court, shame to you.
value.literal: But my strength and wit shallow and short—soon I was seized; above I shame the court, below I fail my friends.

value.zh: 本以名義干心，不得不爾，流腸碎首，復何言哉！
value.en: Duty drove me; guts spill—what more can I say?
value.literal: Originally it was fame and duty that moved my heart—I could not do otherwise; guts streaming, head smashed—what more is there to say!

value.zh: 昔李斯憶上蔡黃犬，陸機想華亭鶴唳，豈不以恍惚無際，一去不還者乎？
value.en: Li Si remembered Shangcai's yellow dog; Lu Ji the crane at Huating—gone, never back.
value.literal: In old times Li Si remembered the yellow dog of Shangcai; Lu Ji thought of the crane's cry at Huating—was it not because illusion has no bound, once gone never to return?

value.zh: 今欲對秋月，臨春風，藉芳草，蔭花樹，廣召名勝，賦詩洛濱，其可得乎？
value.en: I will not face the moon, the wind, the grass, the trees, or poems on the Luo again.
value.literal: Now I wish to face the autumn moon, meet the spring wind, lean on fragrant grass, shade flowering trees, broadly summon famous guests, compose poems on the Luo shore—can it be obtained?

value.zh: 凡百君子，各敬爾宜，為國為身，善勗名節，立功立事，為身而已，吾何言哉！」
value.en: Live for the state and for yourselves; make merit; I have no more words."
value.literal: All you gentlemen, each respect your proper conduct; for the state and for the body, well urge fame and integrity, establish merit and affairs—for the body alone—what have I to say!

value.zh: 時人憐之。
value.en: Men pitied him.
value.literal: People of the time pitied him.

value.zh: 袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 溫子昇
value.en: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng
value.literal: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, Wen Zisheng

value.zh: 夫文之為用，其來日久。
value.en: Literature has served human purposes for a very long time.
value.literal: As for the use of literature, its coming has been long.

value.zh: 自昔聖達之作，賢哲之書，莫不統理成章，蘊氣標致，其流廣變，諸非一貫，文質推移，與時俱化。
value.en: Since antiquity, the writings of the greatest sages and the books of the wisest minds have all been shaped into coherent form, charged with spirit and distinguished by style. Their currents spread and change in many ways rather than following a single line; elegance and plainness evolve as literature keeps pace with the times.
value.literal: From of old the works of sages and worthies and the books of the wise have all been ordered into chapters, imbued with spirit and marked by style; their currents are broad and varied and not of one tradition; substance and ornament shift and transform with the age.

value.zh: 淳于出齊，有雕龍之目；
value.en: When Chunyu emerged from Qi, he possessed the discerning eye celebrated in the title Carving the Dragon;
value.literal: Chunyu came forth from Qi and had the eyes of the Carved Dragon;

value.zh: 靈均逐楚，著嘉禍之章。
value.en: Qu Yuan was banished from Chu and wrote his celebrated piece on the noble orange.
value.literal: Lingjun was banished from Chu and composed the chapter of auspicious calamity.

value.zh: [2]漢之西京，馬揚為首稱；
