value.en: In the Western Capital of the Han, Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong were the leading names;
value.literal: In the Western Capital of Han, Sima and Yang were foremost in renown;

value.zh: 東都之下，班張為雄伯。
value.en: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban Gu and Zhang Heng were the reigning masters.
value.literal: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban and Zhang were the heroic lords.

value.zh: 曹植信魏世之英，陸機則晉朝之秀，雖同時並列，分途爭遠。
value.en: Cao Zhi was truly the genius of the Wei, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though contemporaries, they pursued diverging paths to ever greater distance.
value.literal: Cao Zhi was truly the hero of Wei times, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though standing at the same time, they contested along separate paths to ever greater distance.

value.zh: 永嘉之後，天下分崩，夷狄交馳，文章殄滅。
value.en: After the Yongjia turmoil, the empire fell apart, foreign peoples surged one after another, and literary culture was nearly extinguished.
value.literal: After the Yongjia era, the realm fragmented, barbarians rode in succession, and belles-lettres perished.

value.zh: 昭成、太祖之世，南收燕趙，網羅俊乂。
value.en: Under Emperor Zhaocheng and Emperor Daowu, the court recovered Yan and Zhao in the south and gathered men of outstanding talent.
value.literal: In the reigns of Zhaocheng and Taizu, they gathered Yan and Zhao to the south and netted outstanding men.

value.zh: 逮高祖馭天，銳情文學，蓋以頡頏漢徹，掩踔曹丕，氣韻高豔，才藻獨構。
value.en: When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he threw himself into literature, in spirit rivaling Emperor Wu of Han and outshining Cao Pi, with a lofty tone, brilliant style, and literary gifts all his own.
value.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took Heaven's mandate, he was keen on literature, roughly rivaling Han Wudi, surpassing Cao Pi, with lofty spirit and brilliant ornament and literary talent uniquely formed.

value.zh: 衣冠仰止，咸慕新風。
value.en: Men of culture looked up to him, and all were drawn to the new literary current he set.
value.literal: The gentry looked up and all admired the new style.

value.zh: 肅宗歷位，文雅大盛，學者如牛毛，成者如麟角，孔子曰：「才難，不其然乎？」
value.en: Under Emperor Suzong, literary culture flourished as never before: students were as numerous as ox hairs, but those who truly succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is that not exactly the case?"
value.literal: When Emperor Suzong held the throne, refinement flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is it not so?"

value.zh: 袁躍，字景騰，陳郡人，尚書翻弟也。
value.en: Yuan Yue, whose style was Jingteng, came from Chen commandery and was the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.
value.literal: Yuan Yue, style name Jingteng, was a man of Chen commandery and the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.

value.zh: 博學儁才，性不矯俗，篤於交友。
value.en: He was widely learned and exceptionally gifted, unpretentious by nature, and deeply loyal to his friends.
value.literal: He was broadly learned and outstanding in talent, by nature not given to affectation, and devoted in friendship.

value.zh: 翻每謂人曰：「躍可謂我家千里駒也。」
value.en: Fan often told others, "Yue may truly be called the thousand-li steed of our clan."
value.literal: Fan often said to people, "Yue may be called the thousand-li colt of our house."

value.zh: 釋褐司空行參軍，歷位尚書都兵郎中，加員外散騎常侍。
value.en: He began his career as acting adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose to director of arms in the Ministry of Works, and was later given the additional title of supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
value.literal: He took his first office as Acting Adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose through posts to Director of Arms in the Ministry of Works, and was additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

value.zh: 將立明堂，躍乃上議，當時稱其博洽。
value.en: When the court was preparing to build the Bright Hall, Yue submitted a memorial on the subject, and contemporaries praised his encyclopedic learning.
value.literal: When the Bright Hall was about to be established, Yue submitted a memorial of discussion, and at the time he was praised as broadly versed.

value.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瓌亡破來奔，朝廷矜之，送復其國。
value.en: Anagui, ruler of the Rouran, fled to the court after his state was destroyed; the court took pity on him and helped restore his kingdom.
value.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui, destroyed and fleeing, came to surrender; the court took pity on him and sent him back to restore his state.

value.zh: 既而每使朝貢，辭旨頗不盡禮。
value.en: Afterward, whenever he sent tribute missions, their language was often less than fully respectful.
value.literal: Thereafter, whenever he sent tribute missions, their wording was rather lacking in courtesy.

value.zh: 躍為朝臣書與瓌，陳以禍福，言辭甚美。
value.en: Yue drafted a letter from the court ministers to Anagui, explaining the consequences of fortune and disaster in language of exceptional elegance.
value.literal: Yue wrote on behalf of the court ministers to Gui, setting forth fortune and calamity; the language was very fine.

value.zh: 後遷車騎將軍、太傅、清河王懌文學，雅為懌所愛賞。
value.en: He was later appointed literary aide to Prince Yi of Qinghe, who also held the posts of general of chariots and cavalry and grand tutor, and Yi greatly favored and admired him.
value.literal: Later he was transferred to literary aide to the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Qinghe, Yuan Yi, and was greatly loved and rewarded by Yi.

value.zh: 懌之文表多出於躍。
value.en: Most of Yi's official documents and memorials were written by Yue.
value.literal: Yi's literary memorials and proclamations mostly came from Yue.

value.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、吏部郎中。
value.en: When he died, he was posthumously honored as champion general and director in the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: He died and was posthumously given the titles Champion General and Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 所制文集行於世。
value.en: His collected writings circulated widely.
value.literal: The collected writings he composed circulated in the world.

value.zh: 無子，兄翻以子聿脩繼。
value.en: He left no son; his elder brother Fan had his own son Yuxiu succeed him.
value.literal: He had no son; his elder brother Fan made his son Yuxiu the heir.

value.zh: 蕭衍使張皐寫子昇文筆，傳於江外。
value.en: Xiao Yan had Zhang Gao copy Zisheng's writings, which circulated beyond the Yangtze.
value.literal: Xiao Yan had Zhang Gao copy out Zisheng's writings, which spread beyond the river.

value.zh: 衍稱之曰：「曹植、陸機復生於北土。
value.en: Yan praised him, saying, "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji are reborn in the northern lands.
value.literal: Yan praised him, saying: "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji are reborn in the northern lands.

value.zh: 恨我辭人，數窮百六。」
value.en: I only regret that among my literary men fortune has been broken by repeated calamity."
value.literal: I regret that among my men of letters the count has been exhausted by the cycle of calamity."

value.zh: 陽夏太守傅標使吐谷渾，見其國主牀頭有書數卷，乃是子昇文也。
value.en: Fu Biao, Administrator of Yangxia, on a mission to the Tuyuhun, saw several scrolls at the ruler's bedside—they were writings of Zisheng.
value.literal: The Administrator of Yangxia, Fu Biao, on a mission to the Tuyuhun, saw several scrolls at the ruler's bedside—these were writings of Zisheng.

value.zh: 濟陰王暉業嘗云：「江左文人，宋有顏延之、謝靈運，梁有沈約、任昉，我子昇足以陵顏轢謝，含任吐沈。」
value.en: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said, "Among literati south of the Yangtze, Song had Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, Liang had Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng is enough to stride over Yan and trample Xie, encompass Ren and surpass Shen."
value.literal: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said: "Among men of letters south of the Yangtze, in Song there were Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, in Liang there were Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng suffices to tread upon Yan and crush Xie, swallow Ren and spit out Shen."

value.zh: 楊遵彥作文德論，以為古今辭人皆負才遺行，澆薄險忌，唯邢子才、王元景、溫子昇彬彬有德素。
value.en: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," arguing that writers of every age bore talent yet abandoned proper conduct—shallow, base, treacherous, and jealous—yet only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed genuine virtue.
value.literal: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," holding that men of letters ancient and modern all bore talent yet cast off conduct, shallow, thin, treacherous, and jealous—only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed virtue and plainness.

value.zh: 夫在天成象，聖人是觀，日月五星，象之著者，變常舛度，徵咎隨焉。
value.en: Heaven sets signs in the sky, and the sage is the one who reads them; the sun, moon, and five planets are the clearest of those signs—when the usual order shifts and celestial measures go wrong, omens of calamity follow in their wake.
value.literal: As for Heaven forming signs on high, the sage is one who observes them; the sun, moon, and five stars are the prominent among such signs—when constancy changes and degrees go awry, tokens of blame and misfortune follow.

value.zh: 然則明晦暈蝕，疾餘犯守，飛流欻起，彗孛不恒，或皇靈降臨，示譴以戒下，或王化有虧，感達於天路。
value.en: Whether in brightness or dimness, halos or eclipses, swift planetary crossings or prolonged station-keeping, sudden meteors or unpredictable comets—sometimes the imperial spirit descends to warn the realm below, and sometimes defects in royal governance reach heaven's road.
value.literal: Thus whether bright or dark, halos or eclipses, swift trespass and lingering occupancy, meteor flashes suddenly rising, or comets and broom-stars not constant—sometimes the imperial numen descends, displaying reprimand to warn those below, or sometimes royal transformation is impaired and the response reaches the road of Heaven.

value.zh: 易稱「天垂象，見吉凶」，「觀乎天文，以察時變」；
value.en: The Book of Changes says, "Heaven displays signs revealing fortune and misfortune," and "Look to the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the times";
value.literal: The Changes says, "Heaven displays signs by which fortune and misfortune may be seen," and "Observe the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the times";

value.zh: 書曰「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時」。
value.en: The Book of Documents says, "Mark out the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently give the people their seasons."
value.literal: The Documents says, "Calculate and image the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently bestow the seasons upon the people."

value.zh: 是故有國有家者之所祗畏也。
value.en: This is why rulers of states and clans treat it with reverent awe.
value.literal: Therefore this is what those who possess a state or a clan hold in reverent awe.

value.zh: 百王興廢之驗，萬國禍福之來，兆勤雖微，罔不必至，著於前載，不可得而備舉也。
value.en: The rise and fall of dynasties and the fortune or ruin of nations—even the faintest omen is never empty; the former records are full of them, and no complete list could be given.
value.literal: The proofs of the rise and fall of the hundred kings, the coming of fortune and misfortune to the myriad states—though the portents be slight and subtle, none fail to arrive; recorded in former annals, they cannot all be enumerated.

value.zh: 班史以日暈五星之屬列天文志，薄蝕彗孛之比入五行說。
value.en: Ban Gu's History put solar halos and the five planets in the Astronomical Treatise, but eclipses, comets, and similar phenomena in the discourse on the Five Phases.
value.literal: Ban's History placed solar halos and the five stars and their kind in the Treatise on Astronomy, while thin eclipses, comets, and broom-stars and the like were entered into the discourse on the Five Phases.

value.zh: 七曜一也，而分為二志，故陸機云學者所疑也。
value.en: The seven luminaries are one class of phenomena, yet Ban split them across two treatises—hence Lu Ji's remark that scholars have long found this puzzling.
value.literal: The seven luminaries are one category, yet they were divided into two treatises; hence Lu Ji said that scholars have doubts about this.

value.zh: 今以在天諸異咸入天象，其應徵符合，隨而條載，無所顯驗則闕之云。
value.en: Here all heavenly anomalies are gathered in this Celestial Phenomena treatise; when earthly events confirm the omen, they are recorded in sequence, and where no verification appears, the entry is left blank.
value.literal: Now all celestial anomalies in the heavens are gathered into Celestial Phenomena; where there are corresponding proofs, they are entered item by item as they occur, and where there is no manifest verification, that is omitted.

value.zh: 始，唐興，疏屬畢王，至太宗，稍稍降封。
value.en: When Tang first rose, every distant clansman was enfeoffed as king; by Taizong's reign those titles were gradually reduced.
value.literal: At first, when Tang rose, distant clansmen were all enfeoffed as kings; by Taizong's time enfeoffments were gradually reduced.

value.zh: 時天下已定，帝與名臣蕭瑀等喟然講封建事，欲與三代比隆，而魏征、李百藥皆謂不然。
value.en: Once the realm was settled, the Emperor discussed enfeoffment with eminent ministers such as Xiao Yu, wishing to rival the Three Dynasties—but Wei Zheng and Li Baiyao opposed it.
value.literal: By then the realm was already settled; the Emperor with eminent ministers such as Xiao Yu sighed and discussed enfeoffment, wishing to rival the Three Dynasties in glory, but Wei Zheng and Li Baiyao all said it should not be done.

value.zh: 征意以唐承大亂，民人雕喪，始復生業，遽起而瓜分之，故有五不可之說。
value.en: Zheng argued that Tang had inherited devastation, the people were only just recovering their livelihoods, and to divide the realm anew would be impossible on five grounds.
value.literal: Zheng's view was that Tang inherited great disorder, the people were devastated, and livelihoods had only just revived—suddenly to divide them again was therefore his argument of five impossibilities.

value.zh: 百藥稱帝王自有命，歷祚之短長不緣封建。
value.en: Baiyao held that emperors receive their own mandate and a dynasty's span does not depend on enfeoffment.
value.literal: Baiyao said emperors have their own mandate, and the length of a dynasty's fortune does not depend on enfeoffment.

value.zh: 又舉春秋二百四十二年之禍，亟於哀、平、桓、靈，而詆曹元首、陸士衡之言以為繆悠。
value.en: He also cited the calamities of the Spring and Autumn's 242 years, especially under Ai, Ping, Huan, and Ling, and dismissed the arguments of Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji as absurd.
value.literal: He also cited the calamities of the Spring and Autumn's 242 years, pressing hardest in the reigns of Ai, Ping, Huan, and Ling, and condemned the words of Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji as absurd.

value.zh: 而顏師古獨議建諸侯，當少其力，與州縣雜治，以相維持。
value.en: Yan Shigu alone argued for establishing feudal lords, but with reduced power, governing alongside prefectures and counties to keep one another in check.
value.literal: Yan Shigu alone argued for establishing feudal lords, saying their power should be reduced and they should be mixed in governance with prefectures and counties to hold one another in check.

value.zh: 然天子由是罷不復議。
value.en: Thereupon the Son of Heaven dropped the matter and never raised it again.
value.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven on this account ceased and did not discuss it again.

value.zh: 至名儒劉秩目武氏之禍，則建論以為設爵無土，署官不職，非古之道，故權移外家，宗廟絕而更存。
value.en: Later the scholar Liu Zhi, surveying the Wu clan's seizure of power, argued that granting titles without fiefs and appointing officials without duties was not the ancient way—so power passed to the maternal kin, and though the ancestral line was severed, the dynasty endured.
value.literal: Down to the eminent scholar Liu Zhi, who looked on the calamity of the Wu clan, he set forth the theory that granting titles without fiefs and appointing officials without duties was not the way of antiquity—therefore power shifted to the maternal kin, and though the ancestral temple was cut off, the dynasty yet survived.

value.zh: 存之之理，在取順而難逆；
value.en: Survival, Liu Zhi held, depends on winning compliance and making resistance hard;
value.literal: The principle of survival lies in taking compliance and making opposition difficult;

value.zh: 絕之之原，在單弱而無所憚。
value.en: extinction comes from standing alone, weak, and without anything to restrain challengers.
value.literal: the root of extinction lies in standing alone, weak, and with nothing to fear.

value.zh: 至謂郡縣可以小寧，不可以久安。
value.en: He even argued that the prefectural system might secure brief peace but never lasting stability.
value.literal: He even said that commanderies and counties could bring brief peace but not lasting stability.

value.zh: 大抵與曹、陸相上下。
value.en: Broadly speaking, his argument stood on the same level as Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji.
value.literal: On the whole his view ranked with those of Cao and Lu.

value.zh: 而杜佑、柳宗元深探其本，據古驗今，而反復焉。
value.en: Du You and Liu Zongyuan, however, dug deeper, tested present practice against antiquity, and argued the question through.
value.literal: But Du You and Liu Zongyuan probed the root deeply, tested the present against antiquity, and argued back and forth.

value.zh: 相國倫欲收入望，選用海內名德之士，以前平陽太守李重、滎陽太守荀組為左、右長史，東平王堪、沛國劉謨為左、右司馬，尚書郎陽平束皙為記室，淮南王文學荀嵩、殿中郎陸機為參軍。
value.en: Lun sought esteem and recruited renowned men: Li Chong and Xun Zu as chief clerks; Kan, Prince of Dongping, and Liu Mo as majors; Shuxi as recorder; Xun Song and Lu Ji on staff.
value.literal: Chancellor Lun wished to win esteem and selected men of virtue throughout the realm: the former Administrator of Pingyang Li Chong and Administrator of Xingyang Xun Zu as Left and Right Chief Clerks; the Prince of Dongping Kan and Liu Mo of Peiguo as Left and Right Majors; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Shuxi of Yangping as Recorder; the Literary Scholar of Huainan Xun Song and Palace Gentleman Lu Ji as Staff.

value.zh: 組，勖之子；
value.en: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;
value.literal: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;

value.zh: 嵩，彧之玄孫也。
value.en: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.
value.literal: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.

value.zh: 李重知倫有異志，辭疾不就，倫逼之不已，憂憤成疾，扶曳受拜，數日而卒。
value.en: Li Chong saw Lun's rebellious intent, pleaded illness, was forced to accept office, and died within days of grief.
value.literal: Li Chong knew Lun harbored rebellious intent, declined illness and would not come; Lun pressed him without cease; he fell ill from grief and anger, was carried in to accept appointment, and died within days.
